rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A linear combination of vectors v₁, …, vₙ is any sum x₁v₁ + … + xₙvₙ with real coefficients. Two non-collinear vectors span a plane, three non-coplanar vectors span space; solving for the coefficients is solving a linear system, and uniqueness is exactly linear independence.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Thinking any two vectors span ℝ²; parallel vectors span only a line.  ·  Assuming a representation is unique without first proving the vectors are independent.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: The section formula is an affine combination: coefficients n/(m+n) and m/(m+n) sum to 1.  ·  Centroids use equal weights: the centroid of a triangle with vertices a, b, c is (a + b + c)/3.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Express (4, 5, 6) as a combination of i, j, k: (4, 5, 6) = 4i + 5j + 6k, with coefficients unique because the standard basis is independent.  ·  Check whether (1, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0) and (1, 1, 0) are independent. The determinant of [[1,0,0],[0,1,0],[1,1,0]] is 0, so they are coplanar and dependent: the third equals the sum of the first two.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Independence controls uniqueness, not existence; a spanning set controls existence.  ·  A set containing the zero vector is automatically dependent.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Solve four combination problems  ·  Test three sets for independence

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Put the vectors as COLUMNS of a matrix and row-reduce the augmented system [v₁ … vₙ | r].  ·  For two 2-D vectors, a non-zero determinant x₁y₂ − x₂y₁ immediately proves they span the plane.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Write (5, 3) as a linear combination of (1, 1) and (3, 1).  ·  Determine whether (1, 2, 3), (0, 1, 2) and (0, 0, 1) form a basis of ℝ³.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Write the coefficient equations explicitly before solving; method marks attach to that step.  ·  State whether the representation is unique, and justify it with independence.

rows.label: Classified table
rows.text: Linear combinations — the classified verdicts · Verdict | Condition | Geometric meaning · Expressible | c = alpha a + beta b solves | c lies in the span of a, b · Unique coefficients | a, b non-collinear | One and only one representation · Redundant pair | a, b collinear | Span is a line; many or no representations · Basis use | Non-collinear, non-zero pair | Every plane vector decomposes on it

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Every vector space has a basis, and all bases of a given space have the same number of elements.  ·  The dimension of ℝ³ is 3, so four vectors in ℝ³ are always dependent.

rows.text: Find t so that the point (1 − t)(2, 1) + t(6, 5) is the midpoint of the segment.

rows.text: The vectors (1, 2) and (2, 4) span → B  ·  Coefficients in the representation r = x₁v₁ + … + xₙvₙ are unique when → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Definition.** Given vectors v₁, …, vₙ and scalars x₁, …, xₙ, the vector r = x₁v₁ + … + xₙvₙ is a linear combination of them.  ·  **Span.** The set of all linear combinations of v₁, …, vₙ is their span. In ℝ² two non-collinear vectors span the whole plane; in ℝ³ three non-coplanar vectors span all of space.  ·  **Worked example.** Write (7, 1) as a combination of a = (1, 1) and b = (2, −1): x + 2y = 7 and x − y = 1 give y = 2, x = 3, so (7, 1) = 3a + 2b.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: det[v₁ v₂ v₃] ≠ 0 ⇔ {v₁, v₂, v₃} is a basis of ℝ³  ·  p = (1 − t)a + t b, 0 ≤ t ≤ 1 (segment AB)  ·  In ℝⁿ no more than n vectors can be linearly independent.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: A vector lies in the span of v₁, …, vₙ exactly when the coefficient system is consistent.  ·  Coefficients in a basis are unique.  ·  Three vectors in ℝ³ are independent iff their scalar triple product is non-zero.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: If coefficients must sum to 1, add that equation to the system before solving.  ·  Solve three coefficient systems by row reduction and check each answer by re-substitution.  ·  Find two different coefficient sets for the same vector using a dependent set.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Coefficient system.** Equating components turns r = x₁v₁ + … + xₙvₙ into a system of linear equations; solve by elimination, substitution, or Cramer's rule.  ·  **Existence.** A solution exists iff r lies in the span. Geometrically, if a and b span a plane and r has a component out of that plane, no coefficients exist.  ·  **Uniqueness.** Coefficients are unique exactly when the vectors are linearly independent; with dependent vectors, infinitely many coefficient sets produce the same r.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Linear independence.** v₁, …, vₙ are independent when x₁v₁ + … + xₙvₙ = 0 forces every xᵢ = 0; otherwise one vector is a combination of the others.  ·  **Basis.** An independent set that spans the space is a basis. In ℝ³ the standard basis is i, j, k, and (x, y, z) = xi + yj + zk with unique coefficients.  ·  **Determinant test.** For three vectors in ℝ³, independence is equivalent to the determinant of the matrix with those vectors as rows (or columns) being non-zero; zero determinant means coplanar and dependent.
